content.text:
**What I'd say to my son:**

"I haven't decided anything. I'm going to ask you first, and maybe the bank. The page says the best pair is the **פסגות** account with the fund called **ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500 (4D)**. At the top in big letters it says **86,492 ₪** is left 'בעוד 10 שנים, אחרי דמי ניהול ומס, בכסף של היום'. That's if I put in 10,000 ₪ now and 500 ₪ a month. I'm not sure about it. Leumi is the bank name I know, and on the list it comes second with 83,396 ₪, so not far behind. And I don't understand what Pesagot charges, 'דמי משמרת 699 ₪'. What is that?"

**What I looked at, in order:**
1. The two big numbers at the top: "הפקדתם 70,000 ₪" and "86,492 ₪". I understood that one. I put in 70,000 and get 86,492.
2. "כמה כל בחירה משנה": a picture with lines and little yellow, white and pink marks. I didn't try to read it. I read the sentence under it instead: "בחשבון היקר ביותר נשארים 22,985 ₪ פחות". That one scared me. The wrong place costs 23,000 ₪.
3. On the right, "כל החשבונות": the first three, which are פסגות 86,492, לאומי 83,396 and וואן זירו 83,141. I've never heard of וואן זירו.
4. On the left, the funds. I read the top one, ילין לפידות, "דמי ניהול 0%", and the next one, אלטשולר. I stopped there.

**What I skipped:** all the coloured chips ("צוברת", "מנוטרל מט"ח", "עסקת החלף", "קרן סל", "חשיפה לדולר", "נקנית בחו"ל"…). I skipped the long grey paragraph on the right about "קניה חודשית מחושבת כהוראת קבע", the English line "iShares Core … UCITS ETF", and everything below it.

**Where I hesitated:** the "−43 ₪" and "−213 ₪" next to the funds. Is it a loss? I backed away. Also the "+0.37%" next to "מול המדד". Which מדד? The one on the news?

**What bothered me:** the whole page is black with pale grey writing. It's very busy, full of numbers and colours. Every fund carries the same row of coloured chips, so I had to read them again on each line to find what's different. The little orange and yellow bars next to the accounts have their key written separately, so I had to look back and forth between them. I stopped after this one screen.
